label: <DEL> delimiter step in short sequences (L<=4)
explanation: Fires almost only on the <DEL> delimiter step (99.9% of activation mass; under 0.1% in the copy phase, never in the original phase). Shorter sequences fire more often: about 94% of L=3 delimiters, about 58% of L=4, about 11% of L=5, and almost never for L>=6. L=3 and L=4 together hold about 92% of the mass. Within L=4 and L=5, which tokens are in the sequence decides whether it fires. The highest activations come from sequences whose first tokens are l, g, j, i, v or 3 (e.g. l l z <DEL>), and more digit tokens lowers the firing rate. A first-token list did not beat the simple length rule. It does not fire on original-phase tokens or on long-sequence delimiters.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: i, j, l, v, 3, c; least: q, 1, p, u) and the third original token (most: l, g, z, w, 3, t; least: d, u, f, 1); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=3, L=3, L=4 & t=4.
